transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-05 17:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Staticline Head of ML), Ethan Morales (Staticline Platform Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Staticline PO)
Shared artifacts: Runtime JSON console deck (link: https://redwood.app/briefs/staticline-json-tour), security pack (link: https://redwood.app/sec/staticline-pack.pdf)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
- Quick product tour of Console JSON mode, typed outputs and function calls.
- Discussed runtime guardrails, fallback policies, and Private/VPC deployment constraints.
- Agreed next steps: pilot proposal, perf runs, VPC onboarding.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): all right everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep it tight 45 minutes ish, quick intros?
[00:06] Priya (Staticline): hey thanks, Priya here, we run the ML infra at Staticline, curious mostly about using structured outputs to integrate with our ticketing and orchestration.
[00:12] Ethan (Staticline): Ethan, infra, I'll be the one setting up VPC and network, there's some strict egress rules.
[00:16] Sofia (Staticline): Sofia, product, interested in developer experience and guardrails for customer-facing automations.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood): perfect, Liam and I will do a short console walk, show JSON mode, schema enforcement, function calls, and then the runtime bits — batching, KV caching, prefix caching stuff — and how you can route to cheaper variants.
[00:32] Liam (Redwood SE): quick note — I'll demo the typed response flow and then show how we tie a typed action into an external tool, like a ticketing webhook. There might be a couple of noisy ASR errors in the auto notes, so bear with me.
[00:41] Priya: cool. One ask up front: we care about strict schemas because our downstream systems choke on malformed payloads, so show me failure modes and how Redwood enforces or falls back.
[00:50] Liam: absolutely. We'll show schema validation, typed enums, and a fallback policy where the model can return a minimal safe JSON if it can't meet the schema, then we can route that to a human review queue.
[01:02] Maya: also, security — Priya, is SOC2 and SSO a gating factor?
[01:06] Priya: yes SOC2 compliance and audit logs, and we need KMS integration for keys, ideally customer-managed.
[01:12] Maya: noted, the pack we shared includes our SOC2 cert details and KMS/HSM integrations. For private we support customer KMS and audit log forwarding to your SIEM.
[01:22] Ethan: for VPC, does the private control plane require opening inbound ports? We usually avoid that.
[01:28] Liam: no, our Private plane uses outbound-only peering — think reverse tunnel. You maintain control — you don't need inbound open ports. We'll get the network diagram over. (brief pause)
[01:40] [demo start — Console share audio description]
[01:43] Liam: ok I'm in the console, starting a JSON mode runbook. Top left you can upload a JSON schema, we pick it up and allow live validation in the playground. I'm going to paste a simple schema: order_id as string, priority enum, actions array with typed objects.
[02:01] Priya: can that schema have nested optional fields? Our order documents are multi-level.
[02:05] Liam: yes, arbitrary nesting, optional/required flags, regex patterns. We also support versioned schemas so you can pin a schema to a model rollout.
[02:13] Maya: side note — schema versioning is super useful when you rollout a new model variant and want to detect regressions early.
[02:22] [02:22] Liam: demo — running model in JSON mode, see the left stream is structured output, the runtime validates each token stream and will reject if the final JSON doesn't match. If mismatch, we surface a granular error path like actions[1].assignee missing.
[02:38] Sofia: what happens if the model produces near-miss — e.g., extra field names or slightly wrong enum value?
[02:44] Liam: we have three policies: fail, coerce, or fallback. Fail returns an error with the raw model output and validation hints; coerce will attempt safe casts (e.g., numeric string to int) and report changes in the validation metadata; fallback will emit a compact safe JSON and optionally kick off a tool call to a human review or to a canonicalizer.
[03:02] Priya: show the fallback flow end-to-end?
[03:06] Liam: yep. I'm going to set a fallback rule to call our ticketing tool if validation fails more than 1 time in 30s. Now I invoke a sample prompt that intentionally returns a bad enum.
[03:18] [03:18] model output garbled: "...prioirty: Hight..." (ASR picks up)
[03:24] Liam: notice the runtime catches it, emits an error, then the configured fallback executed a function call to our webhook: POST /internal/tickets with safe JSON payload. You can see the function call trace and the raw tokens that led to the validation failure.
[03:38] Ethan: does the webhook run in our VPC or across the internet? We prefer webhook endpoints inside our network.
[03:44] Liam: the function call is performed from the runtime instance where the model executes. For Private deployments we can place that execution inside your VPC so calls stay internal. For hosted, you can specify a secure tunnel or use an encrypted private endpoint.
[03:58] Maya: wanted to mention token-level debugs — in Console you can enable token tracing for a run and see which tokens correspond to schema failures, it's very helpful for prompt engineering.
[04:11] Priya: excellent. Now, about the optimizer — you mentioned model variants for latency vs cost?
[04:16] Maya: right, Redwood Optimize provides recommended quantization profiles and suggests model family fallbacks. Example: if 1A variant is too slow under load, route to 1B quantized variant with histogram-based quality checks. We can set automatic fallback thresholds.
[04:30] Priya: what's the quality check? Is it semantic similarity?
[04:33] Liam: you can configure a suite of evals — edit distance, embedding cosine on a prompt set, and custom prompts. If quality drops beyond threshold, traffic doesn't route to the cheaper variant and triggers an alert.
[04:45] [04:45] Sofia: can we do canary rollouts for schema changes?
[04:48] Liam: yes — you bind schema versions to rollout policies. Canary 10% for 24 hours, collect validation error rate and structured diffs. If the validation error goes above X% we stop the rollout.
[04:59] Priya: I'm worried about KV cache privacy — our documents contain PII, how is prefix/KV caching handled?
[05:05] Liam: caching is configurable at route level. You can disable KV caching for sensitive routes, or enable encrypted prefix caching with customer KMS so cached KV entries are stored encrypted. Cache TTLs and eviction policies are exposed.
[05:20] Ethan: do you store keys on your side for hosted? We need audit that.
[05:24] Maya: for hosted, we manage caches but can provide audit logs and retention controls; for Private you control storage and KMS keys. We'll put the detailed cache architecture in the follow-up doc.
[05:36] [05:36] demo: showing function call analytics
[05:39] Liam: console shows a graph of function invocations and avg latency, success rate, and mapping to model versions. You can drill into any invocation and replay the exact prompt and model response.
[05:50] Priya: replaying responses — are there redaction tools? We need to scrub PII before storing transcripts.
[05:56] Liam: yes, you can enable inline redaction policies — regex or ML-based PII scrubbers on the ingest path before logs are persisted.
[06:07] Sofia: show a sample of the replay trace for a failure and what fields are returned to non-admins.
[06:12] Liam: good point — RBAC in Console controls field-level visibility. Developers see prompts and validation hints; security sees raw token traces if allowed.
[06:24] [06:24] Maya: switching gears, performance: Ethan, what throughput are you targeting?
[06:28] Ethan: our peak is 1200 rps for short ticket-generation routes, latency SLO 200ms p95 for simple templates.
[06:36] Liam: for those numbers I'd recommend Dedicated capacity with autoscale and a burst pool. Also choose a quantized variant for the fastest path; Redwood's continuous batching should keep p95 low. We'll run a focused benchmark.
[06:48] Priya: about billing — do you bill per token for function calls too?
[06:52] Maya: yes it's per-token for inference plus a small per-invocation function charge for tooling. For Dedicated there are committed capacity plans which amortize token costs. We'll include price breaks in the pilot doc.
[07:05] [07:05] Priya: can you show how the typed action ties into downstream orchestration — e.g., createTicket action -> a microservice?
[07:11] Liam: demo time — creating a typed action spec, binding fields to topic, assignee, priority. Then in the console I map the action to a function integration (we have templates for Jira, ServiceNow, and generic webhooks). I choose webhook template and set an auth token secret from KMS.
[07:29] [07:29] model tries to autocomplete field, small hiccup: it suggested "prioirty" again (laughter).
[07:34] Priya: (laughs) the misspelling seems contagious.
[07:37] Liam: we also show a diff view of generated JSON vs schema and let you accept/coerce changes.
[07:44] Ethan: is there offline validation? We want CI checks on schema changes.
[07:48] Liam: yes, CLI and API validations; you can run schema checks as part of your CI pipeline and fail merges if the example outputs don't validate.
[07:58] [08:00] Maya: quick Q for PII: can you configure anonymization at runtime for certain fields only?
[08:05] Liam: yes, tag those fields in the schema as PII and apply a transform pipeline — redaction, hash, or token replacement. That transform can be done before logs and before tool calls.
[08:18] Priya: show us the perf benchmark plan you'd run.
[08:22] Liam: we'll run three scenarios: 1) simple template generation (short context), 2) multi-turn with KV cache warm, 3) burst loads with mixed sequence lengths. For each we measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, and validation error rate.
[08:36] Ethan: about KV cache warm — how much warmup needed? We have a million small documents.
[08:41] Liam: prefix caching works well for recent hot keys; for a million docs we'd recommend prefetching the hot subset and using tiered cache with TTLs. We'll supply tooling to profile your access distribution.
[08:55] [09:00] Sofia: can we do a small pilot with 10k documents first?
[09:03] Maya: that's usually the sweet spot for POC — small enough to be fast, large enough to surface cache/latency issues. We'll include that in the pilot scope.
[09:12] Priya: what about model drift monitoring?
[09:15] Liam: Redwood Optimize has continuous evaluation — alerting on quality regressions using your prompt set and labeled ground truth. We also surface structured diffs when schema validation rates move.
[09:29] [09:29] Priya: one more legal: audit trail on who changed a schema?
[09:33] Maya: yes, Console has audit logs for schema uploads, who approved rollouts, and time-stamped validation metrics. You can export to your SIEM.
[09:44] Ethan: ok, a couple of nitty-gritty network questions — NAT vs Egress IPs for webhook allowlisting?
[09:50] Liam: for hosted we publish egress IP ranges you can allowlist; for Private we can avoid that by keeping calls inside your VPC.
[09:59] [10:00] demo end — wrap-up and Q&A
[10:03] Sofia: thanks that was helpful. Any gotchas you usually see in pilots?
[10:08] Maya: often teams underestimate schema edge cases — optional nested arrays cause surprises. Also don't assume quantization won't affect certain antonym-heavy prompts — we always include evals for those.
[10:21] Priya: realistic timeline if we greenlight?
[10:24] Maya: paperwork and PO about 2 weeks, pilot provisioning 1 week for Dedicated or 2 for Private VPC networking depending on your IAM approvals. So kickoff mid-Jan is realistic.
[10:36] Ethan: ok I'll share network contacts and a sanitized sample dataset.
[10:40] Liam: I'll prepare the benchmark harness and a template schema that matches your ticket model.
[10:45] Maya: I'll send the commercial pilot terms and security addendum.
[10:49] Priya: great. Any blockers from my side, I'll flag.
[10:53] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the draft SOW. Thanks everyone.
[10:56] (call ends)
